# FormField

Figma: [03j. FormField](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-905) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-26

Composable layout primitives for any form input - Form Field Label (label + optional asterisk + tooltip icon), Form Field Helper (helper text with neutral / error / success / info tones), and Form Field (the wrapper that stacks Label + input slot + Helper with consistent spacing). Use these instead of the per-component Field organisms (Input Field, Select Field, etc.) when you need flexibility - the Form Field slot accepts any input via INSTANCE_SWAP, so the same wrapper can house an Input, a Select, a Switch, a Slider, etc., all with unified label/helper chrome.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/form-field/reference.png`

### Form Field Helper

Helper text with tone color and icon (neutral, error, success, info) shown under a form control.

Level: atom · Part of: Form Field

Use when:
- Validation errors under a field: Tone=error
- Advisory notes such as «يستخدم للتحقق فقط»: Tone=info
- Confirming a check that matters (valid IBAN format): Tone=success

Don't use when:
- Page or form-level messages: use Alert or Banner
- Transient confirmations: use Toast
- Long explanations: use Tooltip from Form Field Label

Accessibility: Tone is shown by icon and color; the text itself must say what is wrong.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Helper text | `helperText` | text |  | Helper text - additional context |
| Tone | `tone` | variant | neutral, error, success, info | neutral |
| Size | `size` | variant | md, sm | md |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | ltr, rtl | ltr |

### Form Field Label

The direction-aware form label atom with optional required asterisk and info tooltip icon; supersedes Input Label for new layouts.

Level: atom · Part of: Form Field

Use when:
- KYC and compliance fields that need a regulatory explanation: Tooltip=true
- Required fields: Required=true
- Labels above custom controls not covered by Form Field

Don't use when:
- Section or page titles: use Section
- Labels already built into Input or Select: do not add a second one

Accessibility: Do not write «(مطلوب)» in the label; use the asterisk and mark the control required in code.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

### Form Field

The layout wrapper that stacks Form Field Label, a swappable control slot and Form Field Helper so any input shares the same label and validation chrome.

Level: organism · Contains: Form Field Label, Input Field, Form Field Helper

Use when:
- Mixed forms where fields use different controls (Input Field, Select, Switch, Slider, Checkbox)
- KYC and bank-details forms needing required marks, tooltips and inline errors
- Success confirmation on a field: State=success

Don't use when:
- The control already includes its own label and helper (Input, Select, Slider Field, TextArea): do not wrap it again
- Grouping several fields under a title: use Section

Accessibility: Label, control and error must be programmatically linked; State does not cascade to the swapped control, so set both.

> Not published to the Figma library. Use it by name everywhere; in another Figma file take its published route or copy it from the Syntropy file (syntropy-components, unpublished.md).

| Size | `size` | variant | lg, md, sm | lg |
| State | `state` | variant | default, error, success, disabled | default |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | ltr, rtl | ltr |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Form Field is the layout system for forms on Safqah. Every input - Input, Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Slider, FileUpload - can sit inside a Form Field wrapper, which provides consistent label placement, asterisk for required fields, optional tooltip help icon, and helper/validation text below.

The atoms (Form Field Label and Form Field Helper) are also independently usable. Reach for them when you need just a label or just a helper without the full wrapper layout - for example, in custom form layouts where the input doesn't fit the standard label-above-input convention.

### At a glance

### Atomic architecture

Three-tier composition: two atoms (Label and Helper) and one organism (Form Field) that stacks them around an exposed input slot.

Atom - Form Field Label · 24 variants

The label primitive. Variants: 3 sizes × Required 2 × Tooltip 2 × 2 directions. Use independently for labels above any custom form element, or rely on the Form Field organism's nested instance.

Atom - Form Field Helper · 16 variants

The helper text primitive with tone-specific iconography. Variants: 4 tones (neutral / error / success / info) × 2 sizes × 2 directions. Use for inline validation feedback, optional-field hints, or contextual help.

Organism - Form Field · 24 variants

The layout wrapper. Variants: 3 sizes × 4 states × 2 directions. Stacks Form Field Label + bare Input Field slot (exposed instance) + Form Field Helper. The input slot can be swapped to any other form component (Select, Checkbox, Switch, Slider, FileUpload) via Figma's instance swap.

### Sizes

Three sizes match the form family conventions. The Form Field wrapper applies the size to both Label (font size adjusts) and Input slot (control height adjusts).

Large (label font 16dp)

Primary forms - KYC, onboarding, deal commitment. Mobile-first. Pair with lg inputs.

Medium (label font 14dp)

Standard desktop density - settings forms, dashboard filters. Most common for desktop UIs.

Small (label font 12dp)

Compact contexts - inline editors, modal forms, dense panels. Avoid on touch-only contexts.

### States

Four states cascade through the Form Field. The State variant controls both the Input slot's appearance (default/error/disabled border) AND the Helper visibility/tone (error shows red helper, success shows green helper).

default

Resting state. Label + bare input + (helper hidden). Used for the majority of form fields where no validation has occurred yet.

error

Validation failed. Input border switches to bg/error (red), Helper appears with red text + alert triangle icon. Use for inline validation feedback.

success

Validation passed. Input border stays default (no green border - design choice to avoid visual noise), Helper appears with green text + check icon to confirm correct input.

disabled

Inert. Input drops to bg/disabled (gray), Label drops to text/muted. Helper stays hidden (no validation message when the user can't edit the field).

### Label variations

Form Field Label has Required and Tooltip toggles via variant axes. These signal field semantics (required vs optional, help available via tooltip) directly in the label.

Plain

Just the label. Use for fields where required/optional is communicated elsewhere (e.g., all fields in a section are required, noted once).

Required

Label + red asterisk. Standard convention for fields that must be filled. Use when most fields in a form are optional and only some are required.

With tooltip

Label + info icon. Use when a field needs additional context that doesn't fit in the helper text (e.g., long explanations, regulatory definitions, examples).

Required + tooltip

Label + asterisk + info icon. Combined for required fields that need extra context (common in KYC and compliance forms).

### Helper tones

Four helper tones cover the full spectrum of feedback messaging. Each tone has its own icon (or none for neutral) and semantic color.

Neutral

Gray text, no icon. Use for static helper text that explains the field's purpose, format hints, or examples (e.g., "Format: YYYY-MM-DD").

Error

Red text + alert triangle icon. Use for validation failures - invalid format, missing required value, value out of range. The most visually prominent helper tone.

Success

Green text + check icon. Use sparingly - confirm specifically when validation matters (strong password met, valid Iqama format confirmed). Don't use for every passing field.

Info

Blue text + info circle icon. Use for non-error advisory messages - "This field is optional", "Used only for verification", "We won't share this".

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Form Field flips its internal alignment for Arabic. Label text right-aligns, required asterisk moves to the leading edge (right), tooltip icon to the trailing edge (left), and the Input slot mirrors. Helper text also right-aligns with the icon on the trailing edge.

LTR

English / default. Label aligned left, asterisk after label, tooltip icon at end. Input fills width left-to-right. Helper aligned left with icon-first.

RTL

Arabic. Label aligned right ("الحقل"), asterisk at trailing edge, tooltip icon at the leading visual edge (left). Input fills width right-to-left. Helper aligned right with text-first, icon at end.

### Composition - swapping the input slot

The Form Field organism has its Input Field slot exposed as a swappable nested instance. In Figma, designers can swap the slot to any compatible form component - Select, Checkbox, Switch, Slider, FileUpload - and the wrapper's Label and Helper continue working.

Default - Input slot

The out-of-the-box composition. Form Field wraps a bare Input Field (no internal label/helper) with the Form Field Label above and Helper below.

Switch slot

Form Field with a Switch in the slot. The Helper is typically hidden for switches (instant-apply pattern).

Slider slot

Form Field with a Slider in the slot. Neutral helper text below provides instruction.

Checkbox slot

Form Field with a Checkbox in the slot. Required asterisk in the label signals legal/regulatory agreement.

> **Warning:** INSTANCE_SWAP caveat: Figma's instance swap works at the component level - you can swap the slot's mainComponent, but the new component's width and the wrapper's spacing have to be compatible. For best results, swap to other form organisms in the same size (lg-to-lg, md-to-md). State doesn't cascade across the swap - set the swapped component's state via its own variant props.

### Code examples

How to consume Form Field in Flutter.

### Flutter - basic Form Field with Input

```dart
// Standard form field - Label + Input + Helper
SafqahFormField(
  label: 'Email address',
  isRequired: true,
  inputSlot: SafqahInputField(
    controller: _emailController,
    placeholder: 'name@example.com',
    keyboardType: TextInputType.emailAddress,
  ),
  // Helper appears only when validation has run
  state: _emailError != null
    ? FormFieldState.error
    : FormFieldState.defaultState,
  helperText: _emailError,
  helperTone: HelperTone.error,
)
```

### Flutter - Form Field with tooltip help

```dart
// Required field with tooltip explaining format
SafqahFormField(
  label: 'Iqama number',
  isRequired: true,
  tooltip: 'Your 10-digit Iqama or Saudi National ID',
  inputSlot: SafqahInputField(
    controller: _iqamaController,
    placeholder: '1234567890',
    keyboardType: TextInputType.number,
    maxLength: 10,
  ),
  state: _iqamaValid
    ? FormFieldState.success
    : FormFieldState.defaultState,
  helperText: _iqamaValid ? 'Valid Iqama' : null,
  helperTone: HelperTone.success,
)
```

### Flutter - slot swap (Switch instead of Input)

```dart
// Form Field with a Switch in the slot
SafqahFormField(
  label: 'Email notifications',
  // No isRequired - switches are optional by nature
  inputSlot: SafqahSwitch(
    value: _emailNotifications,
    onChanged: (v) {
      setState(() => _emailNotifications = v);
    },
  ),
  // Helper provides context, not validation
  state: FormFieldState.defaultState,
  helperText: _emailNotifications
    ? 'You\'ll receive weekly digests and important alerts'
    : null,
  helperTone: HelperTone.info,
)
```

### Flutter - Arabic RTL context

```dart
// Arabic locale - Form Field flips internally
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahFormField(
    label: 'رقم الهوية',  // "ID number"
    isRequired: true,
    tooltip: 'رقم الإقامة أو الهوية الوطنية (10 أرقام)',
    inputSlot: SafqahInputField(
      controller: _idController,
      placeholder: '١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩٠',
    ),
    state: _idError != null
      ? FormFieldState.error
      : FormFieldState.defaultState,
    helperText: _idError ?? 'استخدمه للتحقق من الهوية فقط',
    helperTone: _idError != null
      ? HelperTone.error
      : HelperTone.info,
  ),
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Required field signaling: Use the Required variant of Form Field Label (red asterisk) for fields that must be filled. Pair with aria-required="true" on the input. Show validation errors via the error state with red helper text.
- **Don't** · Required field signaling: Don't rely on placeholder text or label color alone to communicate required. Don't use just an aria-required attribute without the visual asterisk - sighted users miss the cue. Don't use "(required)" in the label text - clutters the line and doesn't scale to RTL.
- **Do** · Inline validation feedback: On validation failure, switch the Form Field to the error state. Input border turns red, Helper appears with red text + alert triangle icon explaining the specific issue. Reading order: label → input → error message all in one tab stop.
- **Don't** · Inline validation feedback: Don't use toast notifications or banner alerts for inline field validation. Don't leave the field in default state after a validation failure. Don't hide validation in a separate error summary at the top of the form - error is anchored to its field.
- **Do** · Arabic RTL forms: RTL direction. Label aligned right ("الحقل"), asterisk at the trailing edge, error helper at the right with text-first and alert triangle at end. Matches native Arabic form conventions.
- **Don't** · Arabic RTL forms: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic contexts. Don't mix LTR labels with RTL inputs - looks broken. Don't use Latin-formatted error messages in Arabic UIs ("Please enter a valid value") - use the translated copy.
- **Do** · Optional field hints: For optional fields that need context, use the neutral or info Helper tone. Example: helper text "We use this only for tax reporting" below an optional Tax ID field. Clarifies why the field is there without making it look required.
- **Don't** · Optional field hints: Don't use the success state to communicate "this field is fine" before the user has actually filled it. Don't use the asterisk for optional fields. Don't leave optional fields without any guidance - users wonder why they're being asked.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** Form Field is the "new way forward" for form layouts in v2. Existing per-component Field organisms (Input Field, Select Field, Slider Field, etc.) remain - they're tighter integrations with their specific input. Use Form Field when you need flexibility across input types in the same wrapper; use the per-component Fields when the input is fixed.

> **Info:** Atomic architecture: Form Field Label and Form Field Helper are NEW atoms that supersede the older Input Label and Input Helper atoms (on page 03a). The new atoms are direction-aware, have tone variants on Helper, and have Required/Tooltip toggles on Label - features the older atoms lack. The older atoms remain for backward compatibility but won't get new features.

> **Info:** Input slot uses the bare Input Field organism (`826:579`) from page 03a, NOT the full Input organism (`828:705`). The bare Input Field has no internal label or helper - the Form Field wrapper provides them. If you swap to other components via INSTANCE_SWAP, they should similarly be "bare" controls without internal label/helper chrome to avoid duplication.

> **Warning:** BOOLEAN property defaultValue gotcha hit again - locked constraint #13. Show Required and Show Tooltip on Label were initially bound via componentPropertyReferences, but the BOOLEAN defaultValue at the set level overrode per-variant visibility. Workaround: removed the visible property references on asterisk and tooltip-icon, and set visibility directly per variant based on the Required/Tooltip variant axes. Same fix on Show Helper for the Form Field wrapper.

> **Warning:** RTL text required manual override per locked constraint #11 - when combineAsVariants merges LTR + RTL components, the TEXT property defaultValue is taken from the first variant. Workaround: removed componentPropertyReferences.characters on RTL variants and set Arabic text directly. Same as FileUpload and Upload Button. Means: runtime overrides of Label/Helper text work on LTR variants but RTL variants have hardcoded Arabic defaults until overridden per-instance.

> **Warning:** Per-tone helper text in LTR variants also required manual override (in addition to RTL fix). The TEXT property defaultValue was taken from the first variant (Tone=neutral), so error/success/info LTR variants all showed "Helper text - additional context" by default. Fixed by removing characters property reference and setting tone-specific English text directly: "Please enter a valid value" (error), "Looks good" (success), "This field is optional" (info).

> **Warning:** INSTANCE_SWAP limitations: Figma supports swapping a nested instance's mainComponent at runtime, but the wrapper's layout (label-to-input gap, input-to-helper gap) is tuned for the default Input Field height. Swapping to dramatically different-height components (e.g., a multi-line text area) will leave odd gaps. Future enhancement: parameterize the gap or auto-detect the slot height.

> **Info:** State doesn't cascade across INSTANCE_SWAP. When you swap the input slot to a Switch, the Switch has its own State axis (on/off/disabled) that you set independently from the Form Field's State (default/error/success/disabled). For coherent state synchronization, the runtime framework code coordinates them - Figma alone shows the visual variants.

> **Info:** Helper visibility logic: Helper is shown ONLY when state is error or success in the Form Field wrapper. Default and disabled states hide the helper. This is intentional - adding a permanent helper area would make every form taller and noisier. If you need persistent helper text for a default field, use the bare Form Field Helper atom and place it manually.

> **Info:** No "Success on input border" design decision: the success state changes the Helper to green but keeps the Input Field border at its default color (not green). Reason: a green border on every successfully-filled field creates visual noise across a form with 10+ fields. The green helper is enough confirmation, anchored to the specific field that needed validation. Trade-off: less prominent success signal vs. less visual clutter.

> **Warning:** FONT WORKAROUND - Same as the rest of the form family. All text uses IBM Plex Sans. Font/Size, Font/Line-Height, and Font/Weight all bound to variables on every text node.
